svg.title: grandparents_house floor plan
svg.text: Plan in metres, north up. Single-storey house on the slope north of the shore road, Haeseong (fictional cove port, Gangwon-do east coast, about 3 h from Seoul by coach).
Main room and courtyard drawn to the Codex key world/keys/grandparents_house/ (wide, reverse) and scripts/ch008.yaml. The west wing is not in the key (dashed).
stepped lane ↓ to the shore road and the harbour (8 min with the cart, ch8)
west wing: not in the key (decided here),
HAESEONG · haeseong_port (not to scale), north up
SEA GATE + six buoys, offshore S of the mouth
Grandpa parks the cart here (ch8, ch9)
stepped lane: 8 min from the bus stop with the cart
1 Gate: plain grey metal double gate centred in the cement
south wall; the stepped lane drops to the road.
2 Glazed wooden sliding doors, four panels, the whole south
side; the courtyard wall hides the sea.
4 Kitchenette: sink at the west end.
6 ch7's kitchen corner: worn counter, wooden cutting board,
7 East window, two panes, cream curtains; fishing float on a
8 Low TV cabinet: small dark TV, potted plant, Haru's dinosaur
9 Bedding alcove (NW): folded bedding in a basket, through an
10 Low wooden table, 1.60 × 0.90 m, five cushions, warm cone
11 Peg by the doors: jackets and Grandpa's cap.
13 Three pots along the east yard wall.
14 Grandpa's cardboard hand cart lives here (decided here).
15 West wing (not in the key): grandparents' room, Haru's

• GM Grandma, WEST end, back to the TV cabinet,
• GP Grandpa, EAST end, back to the east window,
• H Haru (next to Grandma) and T Taeo (next to
Grandpa) on the SOUTH side, backs to the doors.
• N Nib alone on the NORTH side, back to the
kitchenette, facing the way in; kneels upright.
• Main room 5 × 6 m, dark timber beams, warm
amber pendant; courtyard 3 m deep. The sea
gate is NOT visible from inside.
• Screen geography: from the doors (K1) the
TV cabinet is LEFT and the east window
RIGHT, the kitchenette far. From the
kitchen (K2) the TV is RIGHT, the window
beside the fridge (float on the hook).
